title: Actions: Attack, Reckless Attack, Withhold Damage
text:
## Attack (Combat) — Mounted, Unmounted

The most common Action: try to damage the opponent with any Weapon Skill.
- **Distance:** Close Quarters, Normal, Long, Missile
- **Contest:** Weapon Skill vs. opponent's Action.

**Attacking a Horse or Weapon.** You may declare an attack on a rider's horse,
though this is dishonorable between knights (**−1 Honor**); a partial success by
the opponent lets the horse benefit from Shield/Parry Protection. Attacking a
horse from foot negates the −5 Height penalty, but the mounted opponent still
gets their +5 Height Advantage. You may instead target the opponent's **weapon**
to break it: the small target imposes **−5** to Weapon Skill, and a win breaks it
(a sword is knocked from the hand instead).

## Reckless Attack (Combat) — Mounted, Unmounted

An unguarded frenzy; always earns a **check to the Reckless trait**. Famously
Reckless characters must use it unless Prudent wins an opposed roll; Exemplary
Reckless must always use it. If one side Reckless-Attacks and the other Defends,
the two cancel and combat resolves normally.
- **Distance:** Close Quarters, Normal, Long
- **Contest:** Weapon Skill vs. opponent's Action; if the opponent is rolling a
  Weapon Skill they get **+5**. **Neither** side may apply Shield/Parry Protection.
- **Win:** deal **+2D6** Damage (**+6D6** on a critical).

## Withhold Damage (Combat) — Mounted, Unmounted

Deliberately reduce your strike: either withhold a preset number of dice, or use
the flat/butt for half damage (roll normal, halve). Using the flat every blow
dishonors the opponent (**−1 Honor** at end of combat). Only usable with a
normal Attack — never on a Mounted Charge or with thrown/missile weapons.
- **Distance:** Close, Normal, Long — **Contest:** Weapon Skill vs. opponent's Action.

title: Action: Call Squire
text:
Squires stay near their knights but may not be close enough to help immediately.
Declare **why** you are calling — usually one of: **First Aid** (heal wounds),
**New weapon** (brings a requested weapon; the knight re-arms), or **Fresh
horse** (brings a mount). Calling does not instantly accomplish the action —
e.g. First Aid needs the squire to pull the knight from combat and spend several
(**1D6**) minutes treating, possibly removing armor.
- **Distance:** Within hearing range
- **Contest:** None — make an unopposed **Squire Roll** (target = Squire Skill).

**Squire Roll Result:**
- **Critical:** squire acts and proceeds with the desired action **this round**.
- **Success:** squire acts and proceeds **next round**.
- **Fail:** squire does not act; the character may call again next round.
- **Fumble:** squire is nowhere to be seen; may reappear later at the GM's discretion.

title: Action: Disarm
text:
Disarm attempts to knock away the opponent's weapon or object from their grasp.
(Attempts to *wrench or seize and take* a weapon use the **Grapple** Action
instead.)
- **Distance:** Close Quarters, Normal
- **Contest:** Weapon Skill vs. opponent's Action
- **Critical:** the weapon/object flies out of easy reach, or lands at the
  character's feet (character's choice).
- **Win:** the opponent drops the weapon/object within reach; it may be picked up
  as a non-Combat action the following round. If more than one character tries to
  pick it up, resolve with an opposed DEX roll.

title: Action: Grapple, Follow-up Actions (Table 7.3) & Escape
text:
## Grapple (Brawling) — Mounted, Unmounted

A normally two-handed attempt to grab a foe or seize an object from their grip
(one-handed at **−5**). A foot character may Grapple a foe on foot or mounted,
but a mounted character may only Grapple another mounted foe. You may Grapple
**only one** foe at a time.
- **Distance:** Contact or Close Quarters
- **Contest:** Brawling vs. opponent's Action. **On a win, select a Follow-up
  Action from Table 7.3.**

## Follow-up Actions

A successful Grapple can be maintained into later rounds (no re-roll needed unless
the opponent attempts an Escape). Roll your normal Damage dice (**+2D6** on a
critical) and compare the total against the opponent's listed Characteristic/Skill
— the total must **exceed** the target for the action to take effect. This
"damage" ignores armor and normally inflicts no actual damage, **except** if the
roll is **≥ twice the target**, you also inflict your Brawling Damage (ignoring
armor).

**Table 7.3 — Follow-up Actions** (damage must exceed opponent's…):

| Action | Beat | Outcome | Grapple maintained? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disarm | Weapon Skill | Opponent drops weapon | Y |
| Hold | STR | Opponent pinned | Y |
| Lift | SIZ | Opponent lifted into the air | Y |
| Seize Weapon | Weapon Skill + ½ STR | Character takes opponent's weapon | N |
| Tackle | DEX | Opponent taken to the ground & pinned (mounted: 1D6 fall damage) | Y |
| Throw Down | SIZ | Must be Lifted first; thrown for 1D6 (foot) or 2D6 (horseback) damage | N |

Notes: a **Disarm** critical sends the weapon out of reach. A **pinned** opponent
(Hold/Tackle) may only attempt Escape, at **−10/+10**; the grappler may then use
any Follow-up automatically. SIZ ≥ 5× the opponent pins one-handed at no penalty;
SIZ < ⅕ the opponent cannot pin at all. A **Lifted** foe can be carried off
across a horse (lifting a foot foe from the saddle needs character+mount SIZ ≥
1½× the target). **Tackles** between mounted combatants require a Horsemanship
roll to avoid taking fall damage yourself.

## Escape (Act) — Unmounted

A pinned character may try to escape on later rounds: opposed roll of your
**Brawling −10** vs. the opponent's **Brawling +10**. Win → roll "damage" trying
to beat the grappler's STR. Lose → the opponent may execute a Follow-up Action as
normal.

title: Action: Hook
text:
Hook uses a bill, reversed longsword, or hooked farm implement (hoe, rake,
scythe) to snag an opponent and pull them to the ground.
- **Distance:** Any melee distance except Contact
- **Contest:** Weapon Skill vs. opponent's Action
- **Win:** inflict no damage; instead make an unopposed **STR roll** — on success
  it pulls the opponent down (ending the round on the ground) or unseats a rider
  (who takes **1D6** fall damage). On a **critical**, the opponent is
  automatically pulled down.

title: Action: Mounted Charge (+ Charge Opportunities, Lance Fumble Table 7.2)
text:
A Mounted Charge uses a weapon at full gallop. You must ride a combat-trained
horse capable of Charge Damage, not be engaged at the start of the round, and aim
at a specific opponent. Any weapon may be used except one causing Brawling
damage; spears and lances get special bonuses. The charge **must continue in a
Pass-by** regardless of hit or miss (see p. 149).

- **Distance:** Special — at least **six yards apart per charging character**.
- **Contest:** Charge vs. opponent's Action. **+5** if armed with a **couched**
  spear or lance against anyone not using a Long-reach weapon. For any other
  weapon, effective Charge Skill is the **lower** of Charge or the relevant
  Weapon Skill; and effective Charge Skill can **never exceed Horsemanship**.

**Results** (in addition to / instead of Table 7.1):
- **Win:** hit for Weapon Damage **+1D6**, or the horse's **Charge Damage** if
  using a couched spear/lance. Except on a critical, damage dice may not exceed
  the horse's Charge Damage. A critical adds **+4D6**.
- **Partial Success:** a spear, lance, or hafted weapon breaks.
- **Tie:** hafted weapon breaks; if both critical, the horses crash, each taking
  the other's Charge Damage.
- **Fumble:** sword dropped / hafted weapon breaks; a couched spear or lance also
  breaks **and** triggers a Horsemanship roll on **Table 7.2**.

**Charge Opportunities** (large melee, not engaged at round start): roll 1D6 —
**1–3** may Charge a random opponent (if that opponent is also mounted on a
combat horse, roll again to see if they also Charge); **4–6** no opportunity
(engage in normal melee instead).

**Table 7.2 — Mounted Lance Charge Fumble** (roll Horsemanship):
- **Critical:** lance broken; no further ill effects.
- **Success:** lance broken; struck by flying splinters for **1D6** (armor does
  not protect).
- **Failure:** tip buries in the earth and launches you from the saddle; lance
  broken, **2D6** damage (armor does not protect).
- **Fumble:** tip buries and brings down both you and horse; lance broken,
  **3D6** damage (armor does not protect).

title: Action: Self-sacrifice
text:
A Player may declare a Self-sacrifice for the common good (**GM approval
required** to prevent petty use or the loss of key characters like King Arthur).
The player describes their objective and desired outcome, which **succeeds
automatically** — no dice. In return, **the character dies at the end of the
action** and receives **1,000 Glory** for a heroic death, plus normal Glory for
deeds later witnessed or verified.

Limitations:
- It is not carte blanche — the GM maintains drama (e.g. a knight holding a
  bridge buys time, but not enough for the others to leisurely stroll away). The
  GM decides how long pursuers are delayed and need not tell the players.
- Against a **gargantuan** enemy (dragon, huge giant) a kill is **not
  guaranteed**: instead the hero does the equivalent of a **critical success with
  maximum damage, bypassing the foe's armor** (e.g. 4D6 +4D6 crit at max = 48
  points).

title: Action: Set Spear
text:
Set Spear counters a declared or potential **Charge** attack. The character sets
the butt of the spear against or into the ground, angled at the opponent or their
mount. The spear may be one- or two-handed: one hand allows use of a shield;
a **two-handed grip adds +2D6 damage**.

This Action **only works against an opponent using the Charge Skill** — otherwise
it counts as a simple Attack.
- **Distance:** Long
- **Contest:** Spear Skill vs. opponent's Action

title: Action: Trample
text:
Riders of combat-trained horses may Trample **prone** opponents within their
Movement Rate. Even Chivalrous knights may use it in the heat of battle, at least
against armed foes. Horses dislike stepping on objects, which **cancels the
rider's Height bonus** (though the opponent still suffers a penalty).
- **Distance:** Normal
- **Contest:** Horsemanship vs. opponent's Action **−5**
- **Win:** opponent takes a wound using the horse's **normal (non-Charging)
  Damage** (see Table 10.2: Combat Horses).

title: Action: Zigzag
text:
Zigzag is an evasive Action used while moving, effective **only against missile
attacks** (use Dodge for melee). A combatant wearing **no armor gets +5**. You
cannot Zigzag while moving faster than Walking pace.
- **Distance:** Missile
- **Contest:** unopposed Movement Rate roll, made **before** the missile attack.
- **Critical:** opponent takes **−10** to Missile Weapon Skill; you move up to
  full Movement Rate.
- **Success:** opponent takes **−5**; you move up to half Movement Rate.
- **Failure:** no modifier; you move up to half Movement Rate.
- **Fumble:** no modifier; you stumble and lose all Movement Rate this round.

title: Combat Actions — Overview & Classifications
text:
A **Combat Action** is anything a character chooses to do during a Combat Round.
The list below is the most common options; Gamemasters should ad-lib new ones
using these as a model.

**Action classifications:**

- **Act** — a non-Combat action (often a Characteristic or non-Combat Skill
  roll) that affects combat but does not damage the opponent.
- **Brawling** — damages/affects an opponent at Contact or Close Quarters,
  unarmed or with small/improvised weapons.
- **Combat** — damages/affects an opponent at Close Quarters or greater distance.
- **Communication** — conveys information; usually no die roll.
- **Follow-up Action** — triggered by a successful Grapple.

**Actions list:**

- *Mounted or Unmounted:* Attack, Call Squire, Claim a Prisoner, Defend, Disarm,
  Evade, Mount Up, Pick Up, Reckless Attack, Self-sacrifice, Study, Withhold
  Damage, Zigzag
- *Exclusively Unmounted:* Dodge, Don Armor, Hook, Set Spear
- *Exclusively Mounted:* Control Mount, Mounted Charge, Trample
- *Brawling:* Barehand Attack, Escape, Grapple, Slam

Each definition lists a **Distance** and a **Contest**; a **Results** subheading
appears only when outcomes differ from Table 7.1.

title: Brawling: Barehand Attack & Slam
text:
**Brawling Skill** applies whenever a character fights unarmed or with an
improvised weapon (e.g. a musical instrument) or small weapon (knife, dagger). It
always inflicts the character's **Brawling Damage**, though the weapon/object may
modify this. Brawling also covers grapples, slams, and escapes (see separate
entries).

## Barehand Attack (Brawling) — Mounted, Unmounted

Functions like Attack but uses the **Brawling Skill** instead of a Weapon Skill;
also used for daggers/improvised weapons. Unarmed strikes are a **punch** (closed
fist) or **slap** (open hand).
- **Distance:** Contact or Close Quarters
- **Contest:** Brawling vs. opponent's Action
- **Win:** Brawling Damage for a punch/brawling weapon, or half for a slap; a
  **critical adds +2D6**. Weapons inflict Brawling Damage + their bonus, and add
  the normal **+4D6** on a critical.
- **Fumble:** stumble (**−5** next round); improvised/wooden weapons break;
  daggers are dropped.

## Slam (Brawling) — Unmounted

Hurl your mass into an opponent at speed. Both combatants must be on foot. A foe
with the right weapon may respond with **Set Spear** if they see it coming from
Long distance.
- **Distance:** Close Quarters (**−5**), Normal, or Long (**+5**). Using a shield
  adds **+5**.
- **Contest:** Brawling vs. opponent's Action
- **Win:** roll damage normally (crit **+4D6**) but apply only **Brawling Damage**
  as a wound (armor protects normally). If total damage rolled **> opponent's
  SIZ**, both fall; if **> twice SIZ**, only the opponent is knocked prone.

title: Charge Distance
text:
An effective charge requires a minimum distance of **six yards** between
character and opponent to build enough deadly speed and momentum. A character
and opponent who are **charging each other** must start at least **twelve yards**
apart.

The maximum distance for a Mounted Charge is the horse's Movement Rate, at a
gallop, in one Combat Round. See *Chapter 10: Horses* for the Movement Rates of
horses and other mounts.

title: Combat Modifiers
text:
Circumstances apply bonuses or penalties. Against a single foe all modifiers
always apply; against multiple foes, different modifiers may apply per opponent.
**All modifiers are cumulative.**

- **Cover** — an obstacle (tree, bush, low wall) partially protecting a character
  in melee gives **both** combatants **−5**.
- **Height Advantage** — fighting from height (horseman vs. foot, rampart vs.
  climber, standing vs. prone) gives a **+5/−5 reflexive** modifier in the taller
  combatant's favor. Negated if an unmounted combatant uses a two-handed spear or
  halberd against a mounted foe. A mounted combatant using any weapon **except a
  spear cannot strike a prone opponent**. Missile attacks do not benefit.
- **Strike from Behind** — when the opponent doesn't know an attack is coming:
  an unopposed Attack at **+5** (usually dishonorable; may cost Honor).
- **Immobile Target** — grappled, entangled, stuck, etc.: **−10/+10 reflexive**
  to all actions needing freedom of movement.
- **Surprise** — a wholly unprepared opponent grants the attacker **+5** to
  Weapon Skill for the first round. A missile attack from Surprise ignores the
  target's shield penalty.
- **Visibility** — darkness, fog, or smoke penalizes all Combat Actions (see the
  Awareness skill, p. 98).

title: Combat Movement (Step Five)
text:
Characters who declared movement **other than a charge** now simultaneously move
up to their Movement Rate in yards. A character need not move their full rate,
but **once they choose to stop, they cannot move further** that round.

Movement decides whether a character has closed with an enemy so they may
engage. Once two combatants are within one yard of each other, melee combat is
possible. Except for charges, **all movement takes place at the end of the
Combat Round**.

title: The Combat Round
text:
The **Combat Round** is the basic time measure for single or small-group combat:
a short, elastic unit — the time to conceive of and perform one action in melee.
Rounds continue in succession until everyone is done fighting (through
incapacitation, death, surrender, or flight).

Each character is limited to **one action per round**. This is a loose limit: a
round is not merely a single blow but an exchange of attacks, parries, and
maneuvering. A roll made as a *reaction* to another (e.g. the DEX roll when your
Knockdown value is exceeded) is a **free action** and does not count as your
action for the round.

**Combat Round procedure** — both combatants simultaneously follow, each round:

1. **Declare Combat Actions**
2. **Resolve Combat Actions**
3. **Winner's Outcome**
4. **Loser's Outcome**
5. **Combat Movement**

**Step One — Declare.** All combatants state what they intend to do, the weapon
they wield, and their targets/opponents. Combatants within one yard of each
other are automatically **engaged** and need not move to fight. If timing
matters (e.g. one sets a spear while the other makes a Mounted Charge), resolve
conflicting declarations with opposed DEX rolls — declarations are made from
**lowest DEX to highest**, and the winner resolves first in Step Two.

**Step Two — Resolve.** Any Skill/Combat Skill resolution is made now.
Characters can either fight *or* move, not both — except a **Mounted Charge**,
which combines movement and attack and is resolved here (splitting into two
actions halves the Skill used in each). If combat occurs, both combatants roll
their modified Combat Skills using opposed resolution and consult **Table 7.1:
Combat Action Resolution Results**. Some actions (e.g. Dodge, Disarm) supersede
that table, as noted in the action's definition.

title: Damage & Wounds (Loser's Outcome)
text:
Record damage taken (after subtracting Protection) in the Wounds section of the
character sheet and subtract it from Total Hit Points. Note each wound
**separately** — First Aid is applied to each individually — and check what type
was inflicted (Minor, Major, or Mortal).

- **Major Wound:** if actual damage **equals or exceeds the loser's CON**, they
  suffer a Major Wound and fall unconscious.
- **Unconscious:** if Current Hit Points fall **below the Unconscious
  Characteristic**, the loser falls unconscious. They are out of the fight until
  First Aid raises Current Hit Points to at least their Unconscious value.
- **Mortally Wounded:** if Hit Points drop to **0 or less**, the character will
  die if not quickly rescued.

If **mounted** when knocked unconscious or Major-Wounded, the character may
attempt an **Emergency Dismount** (unopposed DEX roll): success = a gentle fall
doing little or no damage; failure = a bad fall causing **1D6** damage.

See *Chapter 11: Injury and Health* for wound effects and recovery.

title: Actions: Defend, Dodge, Evade
text:
## Defend (Act) — Mounted, Unmounted

Forgo damage in favor of protecting yourself. A smart choice against
overwhelming odds.
- **Distance:** Any melee distance
- **Contest:** Weapon Skill **+10** vs. opponent's Action
- **Win or Tie:** take no damage, deal no damage.

## Dodge (Act) — Unmounted

Throw yourself aside to avoid damage. Your single roll is pitted against **all**
opponents' rolls and forgoes the usual multiple-opponents penalty. Usable at any
distance against melee attacks, but you must be on your feet. **Melee only — use
Zigzag for missiles.**
- **Distance:** Any melee distance
- **Contest:** Movement Rate vs. opponent's Action
- **Critical:** avoid damage, deal none, and begin next round ready to act.
- **Win:** avoid damage, deal none, but start next round on the ground (weapon
  still in hand).
- **Lose:** take all damage; start next round on the ground (weapon in hand).
- **Fumble:** take all damage, fall, start on the ground next round having
  dropped your weapon.

## Evade (Act) — Mounted, Unmounted

Disengage from melee. Like Dodge, negates and deals no damage, and also carries
you **away** from combat.
- **Distance:** Any melee distance
- **Contest:** Movement Rate (horse's, if mounted) vs. opponent's Action
- **Win:** neither take nor deal damage; no longer engaged.
- **Fumble:** fall, start next round on the ground; if mounted, fall from the
  horse and take **1D6** damage.

title: Dropped or Broken Weapon
text:
A loser who **fumbles** their opposed weapon roll drops their sword or breaks
their non-sword weapon; the unfortunate character must start the next round
unarmed.

- **Swords** break all non-sword weapons other than daggers **on a tie**.
- A sword breaks **any** weapon, including another sword, when the loser fumbles
  and the winner criticals.

title: Example: Full Combat (worked example — pointer)
text:
A multi-round worked example (Sir Clydno ambushed by a gang of robbers while
mounted) demonstrating how actions and modifiers interact: Passion rolls
(Impassioned +10), Mounted Charge against multiple foes, the on-foot-vs-mounted
−5 penalty, Height Advantage, and Multiple Opponent penalties.

Not transcribed here — this is narrative illustration rather than rules. Consult
the Core Rulebook pp. 153–158 directly if you need the step-by-step walkthrough.
The mechanics it exercises are captured in [[core.combat.combat-round]],
[[core.combat.multiple-opponents]], [[core.combat.combat-modifiers]], and
[[core.combat.action-mounted-charge]].

title: Determining Knockdown
text:
Whenever a character takes a blow (from a weapon or another source, such as
riding into a tree limb), the **base damage** — damage before armor, rebated
weapons, or other reductions — is compared to their **Knockdown value**, which
equals their **SIZ** Characteristic.

- If damage received is **greater than Knockdown**, the character makes an
  unopposed **DEX roll** (whether on foot or mounted); multiple knockdowns in a
  round each require their own roll.
  - **Critical or success:** stays upright / in the saddle, no penalty.
  - **Failure or fumble:** knocked down — begins next round on the ground. If
    mounted, suffers **1D6** damage from the fall and drops their weapon.
- If damage is **greater than twice Knockdown**, the character is
  **automatically** knocked down (mounted: fall, 1D6 damage, drop weapon).
- If damage is **greater than the horse's SIZ**, the horse may be knocked down
  too — see "Horse and Rider Knocked Down" (p. 150).

title: Melee Distances
text:
Distances in melee vary according to the positions of combatants and their
weapons. Some actions require sustained physical contact, some weapons are only
effective at close quarters, and some weapons are so long they are effective
outside of normal melee distances.

Distances are expressed as one of **five qualitative categories**: Contact,
Close Quarters, Normal, Long, and Missile.

Characters may declare at which distance they wish to engage their opponent as
part of their action declaration; otherwise the Gamemaster determines it. When
combatants are within one yard's distance of each other, melee combat is
possible. To avoid combat and move past the enemy, Evasion may be necessary.

title: Missile Distances
text:
Missile ranges are:

- **Short** — up to 30 yards
- **Medium** — 31 to 100 yards
- **Long** — 101 to 200 yards

See "Missile Ranges" (p. 152) for additional rules.

title: Missile Weapons (ranges, modifiers, closing distance)
text:
Knights consider using missile weapons against other knights **cowardly** — a
knight gets a **Cowardly check and loses 1 Honor** for using a bow or crossbow
against another knight in single combat. (Crossbows in a besieged garrison are
acceptable.)

**Missile Ranges & penalties:**
- **Short** — up to 30 yards; the max range for all thrown weapons except javelins.
- **Medium** — 31–100 yards; **−5** to Weapon Skill; max range for javelins.
- **Long** — 101–200 yards; **−10** to Weapon Skill.

**Shielded Targets.** A shield-bearer aware of being targeted imposes the
shield's **Missile Attack Penalty** (e.g. kite shield **−10**) on the archer. The
archer may apply it to shots at the **mount** instead, but loses their own
shield's benefit that round. Shield/Parry Protection points otherwise do not
apply to missile fire.

**Cover** (targets on foot behind cover): Light **−5** (brush, moderate rocks),
Moderate **−10** (low wall, dense trees), Significant **−15** (arrow slit).

**Other Modifiers:** stationary opponents reduce range penalties by 5; Zigzag
**−5** (or **−10**); Surprise **+5**; wind — light 0, irregular **−5**, strong
constant **−10** (wind does not affect hand-hurled weapons).

**Closing Distance (Table 7.5)** — rounds to cross each band; compare to the
weapon's rate of discharge for shots before the attacker arrives. Zigzagging
attackers always use Walking Rate.

| Pace | Short (≤30) | Medium (31–100) | Long (101–200) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Walking | 2 | 4 | 6 |
| Jogging | 1 | 2 | 4 |
| Running | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| Walk (mount) | 2 | 4 | 6 |
| Trot | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| Canter | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| Gallop | 1 | 1 | 1 |

**Other considerations:** *Loosing into a Melee* — equal chance to hit every
combatant; the GM assigns the target at random. *Mounted Targets* — roll 1D6:
**1–4** hits the mount, **5–6** the rider. *Visibility* — adverse conditions may
require an Awareness roll to see the target before shooting. *Water* — a wet bow
or crossbow gives **−5** Weapon Skill, **doubles** all effective ranges, and
**halves** damage.

title: Mounted Combat
text:
Pendragon centers on the mounted knight. See also the Control Mount, Mount Up,
Mounted Charge, Trample, and Zigzag actions.

**Horsemanship Limitation.** Horsemanship limits the **base value** of all Weapon
Skills used while riding; modifiers (combat, Passions, etc.) still apply and can
push the effective value back above Horsemanship. *E.g. Sword 17 with
Horsemanship 15 → effective 15 while mounted; a +5 mounted-vs-foot modifier then
raises it to 20 against that foe.*

**Pass-by.** A Mounted Charge always overshoots the target by a Pass-by distance
(the horse's motion after impact). Minimum distance to rein in = **half** the
horse's normal Movement Rate (the rider may circle to start next round in Normal
range); maximum = the horse's **gallop** Movement Rate minus the distance to
reach the target. On a Win or mutual miss the rider sets the distance; on a Tie
(double success), Partial, or Loss the maximum is **halved and the rider must go
the full distance**. A dismounted rider's horse gallops on for the maximum; if
the horse is knocked down or falls, no Pass-by occurs.

**Mounted Knockdown.** Normal Knockdown rules apply: total damage over SIZ → DEX
roll to stay in the saddle; over **twice SIZ** → automatically thrown. Falling
from the saddle causes **1D6** damage.

**Horse and Rider Knocked Down.** If total damage to *either* horse or rider
exceeds the **horse's SIZ**, the horse makes a DEX roll to stay standing; failure
knocks it down. The rider may attempt an Emergency Dismount; if that also fails,
the rider is **crushed** by the falling steed for the horse's normal Damage
(armor protects normally).

**Emergency Dismount** (unopposed Horsemanship roll — **Table 7.4**):
- **Critical:** land on feet, upright next round, no damage, keep all weapons.
- **Success:** land on feet, upright next round, no damage, but **drop** held weapons.
- **Failure:** improper dismount, **1D6** damage, drop all weapons.
- **Fumble:** **2D6** damage, drop all weapons; if the horse fell, it lands on
  the rider for the horse's Damage.

**Escaping from Under a Fallen Horse.** Each round roll the rider's **STR vs. the
horse's SIZ**; each helper adds +5 to the strongest person's STR (who rolls).

**Limited Two-handed Mounted Weapons.** From horseback, only a **longsword** and
a **two-handed spear** may be used two-handed; other two-handed weapons are too
unbalanced and risk unhorsing the rider.

**Too Big for Your Horse.** Compare the horse's STR to the rider's **SIZ×2**
(subtract 5 if unarmored). If that total exceeds the horse's STR: **−5**
Horsemanship, **−5** horse Movement Rate, treated as Forced March on long travel,
and horse Damage **−1D6**. If the rider's SIZ equals the horse's STR, the horse
cannot bear them at all.

title: Actions: Control Mount, Mount Up
text:
## Control Mount (Act) — Mounted

Get an unruly mount under control before another Action. See "Controlling Horses
in Combat" (p. 181).
- **Contest:** Unopposed Horsemanship roll (**−5** for non-combat-trained horses;
  further penalty equal to Hit Points the horse has lost to wounds).

A horse not trained for combat (any from Table 10.3: Riding Horses) forces a
Horsemanship roll at **−5** at the start of each round: **success** = control +
another action this round; **critical** = controlled for the rest of combat
unless wounded; **failure** = no other action this round; **fumble** = thrown,
must make an Emergency Dismount (p. 150). When any horse takes **5+ points** of
damage in a round, check injury effects; thereafter roll Horsemanship each round
(penalty = total HP lost) before acting — a combat-trained horse settles on a
critical *or* regular success.

## Mount Up (Act) — Mounted, Unmounted

Takes one Combat Round to mount/dismount, unless a squire holds the reins, or you
roll Movement Rate (capped by Horsemanship) to leap into/out of the saddle and
act the same round. Mounting under blows uses an opposed roll (capped by
Horsemanship) vs. the opponent's Action.
- **Win:** mount up, take no damage.
- **Partial Success:** mount up but take damage; no shield/parry protection.
- **Loss:** remain unmounted and take damage; no shield/parry protection.
- **Fumble:** fall; start next round on the ground.

title: Multiple Opponents & Modifier Stacking
text:
Up to **three unmounted** (or **two mounted**) characters may attack one
opponent, since horses take up more space. A character facing several foes must
perform the **same action** against each and applies the Multiple Opponent
modifier separately per action.

**Multiple Opponent Modifier:** a cumulative **−5 per opponent after the first**
(two foes = −5 each; three = −10). Each action is resolved separately. A
character may instead **ignore** one or more opponents — each ignored opponent
gets an unopposed action, but imposes no −5.

**Charging Multiple Opponents** (GM approval): a Mounted Charge may hit several
close foes if they are all within the horse's gallop Movement Rate, in a roughly
straight line, each making an opposed roll, and the weapon isn't broken (a broken
weapon ends the run). The Multiple Opponent modifier applies to all rolls, with
**no cap** on targets.

**Modifier order:** apply **Personal Modifiers** first (they form the base the
Multiple Opponent modifier acts on) — these are **+10 from Defend** and magical
effects. Then apply the Multiple Opponent modifier. Then apply **Situational
Modifiers** (all Combat Modifiers, and Passion modifiers), which affect only the
specific opponent being fought.

title: Armor, Shield, and Parry Protection
text:
Armor and shields absorb damage; parries block it. All are expressed as a
**Protection value**.

The actual damage the loser takes is the difference between the **winner's
damage total** and the loser's **Armor Protection value**.

If the loser rolled a **partial success**, they may *also* apply the **Shield or
Parry Protection value** of their shield/weapon on top of Armor.

title: Re-Arming
text:
In combat, shafts are shattered and swords are dropped on a regular basis. How
long it takes to re-arm is circumstantial and subject to the Gamemaster's
ruling, but here are some guidelines:

- A character with a **sheathed sword or dagger** at their side may draw it at
  the start of a Combat Round without penalty. Weapons in any other location
  (strapped across the back, hung from a saddle or belt, etc.) impose a **−5
  penalty** to your Combat Action that round.
- Characters **on foot** may retrieve a dropped weapon within easy reach; this
  takes a Combat Action and may be opposed (see "Pick Up", p. 141).
- **Mounted** characters who drop a weapon may not retrieve it without
  dismounting first.

Re-arming with a weapon brought forth by your squire requires the **"Call
Squire"** Action (p. 138). You may drop any weapon or shield without taking a
Combat Action — so a knight who charges with their lance on the first round may,
at the start of the second round, drop the lance, draw their sword, and still
Attack.

title: Table 7.1 — Combat Action Resolution Results
text:
Both combatants roll their modified Combat Skill (opposed). Cross-reference the
character's result (rows) against the opponent's result (columns). "+4D6" marks
a critical, which adds the attacker's base Damage dice again. "no Shield/Parry"
means only Armor Protection applies (the loser did not achieve a partial
success). Damage is always reduced by the defender's Protection value.

| Character ↓ / Opponent → | **Critical** | **Success** | **Partial** | **Fail** | **Fumble** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Critical** | Tie: both suffer (Damage − Armor + Shield/Parry) | n/a | Char wins: opp suffers +4D6 − Armor + Shield/Parry | Char wins: opp suffers +4D6 − Armor (no Shield/Parry) | Char wins: opp suffers +4D6 − Armor (no S/P) **& drops/breaks weapon** |
| **Success** | n/a | Tie: both suffer (Damage − Armor + Shield/Parry) | Char wins: opp suffers Damage − Armor + Shield/Parry | Char wins: opp suffers Damage − Armor (no S/P) | Char wins: opp suffers Damage − Armor (no S/P) **& drops/breaks weapon** |
| **Partial** | Opp wins: char suffers +4D6 − Armor + Shield/Parry | Opp wins: char suffers Damage − Armor + Shield/Parry | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| **Fail** | Opp wins: char suffers +4D6 − Armor (no S/P) | Opp wins: char suffers Damage − Armor (no S/P) | n/a | Both lose: neither suffers Damage | Both lose: neither suffers Damage; **opp drops/breaks weapon** |
| **Fumble** | Opp wins: char suffers +4D6 − Armor (no S/P) **& char drops/breaks weapon** | Opp wins: char suffers Damage − Armor (no S/P) **& char drops/breaks weapon** | n/a | Both lose: neither suffers Damage; **char drops/breaks weapon** | Both lose: neither suffers Damage; **both drop/break weapon** |

The winner then resolves **Step Three: Winner's Outcome** — rolling Damage dice
equal to their Damage Characteristic (a critical adds +4D6).

title: Actions: Claim a Prisoner, Pick Up, Don Armor, Study
text:
## Claim a Prisoner (Act) — Mounted, Unmounted

It takes a full Combat Round to accept a foe's surrender, during which you may
take no other action.

## Pick Up (Act) — Mounted, Unmounted

Retrieve something within reach not worn by/attached to another person or object.
Use your hands, or use a spear/lance to pick up small objects from horseback.
- **Distance:** Contact, Close Quarters, Normal
- **Contest:** Unopposed = automatic success; if opposed, roll **DEX+5** vs.
  opponent's Action.

## Don Armor (Act) — Unmounted

Putting on armor takes more than one round; the time depends on armor type and
whether a squire/knight assists (see "Armoring Up", p. 169). Each round donning
armor must be devoted to nothing else. If forced to fight before finishing, you
count as **unarmored**.

## Study (Act) — Mounted, Unmounted

Look over the combat area to see who is prone, wounded, or faring well; the GM
describes the scene, with more detail the more rounds you spend. Obscured things
may require an immediate Awareness roll (with penalties). If attacked while
Studying, you may cancel it for another Action at **−5** for the first round.

title: Winner's Outcome
text:
In an opposed melee exchange, the combatant with the higher **successful** roll
is the winner and resolves their outcome first.

**Step Three: Winner's Outcome.** The winner rolls a number of dice equal to
their Damage Characteristic. A **critical success adds +4D6** to the Damage for
that round (i.e. the base Damage dice are rolled again on top of the weapon
dice — e.g. 5D6 becomes 5D6+4D6). Armor Points (plus any shield) are subtracted
from the total; the remainder is applied to the loser's Hit Points.

**Step Four: Loser's Outcome.** The loser takes the winner's damage, and then:

- **Critical or success:** the loser stays mounted / keeps their footing.
- **Failure or fumble:** the loser is knocked down.

A loser who **fumbles** their opposed weapon roll may have their weapon broken:
swords break all non-sword weapons other than daggers on a tie.
